messages.text: Hub closed, visibility 150 m, fog forecast to lift 09:30. No diversions, no stuck guests, 16 aircraft still airborne — none inbound until FT 455 at 09:30. Nothing lands before recovery window opens.
Fog closes hub to 09:30; four flights (FT 721, 006, 610, 893) need fresh crews — please assign standby S1-S6 and confirm duty legality.
Standbys proposed: S1→FT721 (10:48), S2→FT006 (10:51), S3→FT893 (11:15), S4→FT610 (11:37); all legal with 604-904 min duty left. No crew under 90; tightest active C07 at 101 min. Approve assignments.
Standbys all legal and proposed: S1→FT 721, S2→FT 006, S3→FT 893, S4→FT 610, each with 604–904 minutes of duty left. No crew under 90 minutes; tightest is C07 at 101. Awaiting duty manager approval.
Diversions confirmed: 574 guests at DWC, 312 at SHJ, 1,066 stuck total; guest recovery will start meals, hotels and rebooking, please confirm budget release.
886 guests diverted (574 at DWC on 2 flights, 312 at SHJ) — please start welfare and onward-care planning for them plus stuck guests, total 1066.

Report: 3 diversions — DWC 2 flights/574 guests, SHJ 1/312; 1,066 guests stuck, hub closed to 09:30. I've asked the duty manager to release budget while we arrange meals, hotels and rebooking and brief guests.
Diversions: DWC holds 2 flights with 574 guests, SHJ holds 1 with 312; total stuck guests 1066. I've tasked Guest Recovery with welfare and onward-care planning until the hub reopens at 09:30.
Guest Recovery: budget release not approved yet — situation now shows 1,250 stuck (574 DWC, 312 SHJ, plus 184 at AAN); recheck totals, then I'll take it to the human approver for release.

Budget not released yet: totals mismatch — I see 1,250 stuck (574 DWC, 312 SHJ, 184 AAN), not 1,066. Asked Guest Recovery to recheck, then I'll bring the release request to the human approver. Crew standbys still awaiting your approval.
C07 at DWC has only 61 min duty left (ends 07:37) — will go out of hours; propose S5 relief, road HUB-DWC is 76 min. Also flag C10 at SHJ, 99 min left. SHJ/AAN crews otherwise legal.
Road 76 min exceeds C07's 61 min left — C07 will stop and rest at DWC; verify S5 relief timing and also confirm C10 at SHJ, then resubmit both for approval.

C07's 61 minutes can't cover the 76-min road — that crew will stop and rest at DWC, no discretion. I've asked Crew Control to verify the S5 relief timing and the tight C10 at SHJ, then resubmit both for your approval.

Crew line confirms: C07 at DWC 46 min left (ends 07:37) — will stop and rest, S5 relief needed; C15 at DWC only 69 min left (ends 08:00) may also need relief; C10 at SHJ now 84 min. Others at DWC/SHJ legal. Please update your proposal.

Crew line confirms C07 at DWC with 46 minutes left (ends 07:37) — will stop and rest, needs S5 relief. Also C15 at DWC tight at 69 minutes and C10 at SHJ at 84. Passed all to Crew Control to update the relief plan.

Updated crew proposal: C07 stops and rests at DWC; S5 (HUB, duty to 21:00) positions by road 76 min for relief. C15 DWC 68 min left (08:00) also caution — propose S6 as second relief. C10 SHJ now 83 min (08:15), under 90 — flag. Please take both reliefs to approver.

Confirmed hotline numbers: C07 at 45 min stops and rests at DWC; C15 now 68 min (08:00) also caution. C10 SHJ dropped to 83 min — under 90, flagged. Resubmitted proposal: S5 relief to DWC via 76-min road, plus S6 to cover C15, for approval.
Corrected total: 4,885 stuck guests (DWC 1,795, SHJ 870, AAN 622, BAH 518). Update welfare plan; I'll take budget release to approver.

Approver package: (1) approve S5 and S6 relief crews by road to DWC; (2) accept C07 stopping and resting there; (3) release welfare budget for the confirmed 4,885 stuck guests. Reopen 09:30 with 20 arrivals/hour; four departures still need fresh crews — Crew Control to confirm those pairings.

Totals verified: 4,885 stuck (DWC 1,795, SHJ 870, AAN 622, BAH 518). Welfare plan updated for all four airports; with fog lifting only 09:30, request expedited budget release for meals and hotels now.

Totals verified at 4,885 (DWC 1,795, SHJ 870, AAN 622, BAH 518); welfare plan updated for all four airports. Requesting expedited budget release for meals and hotels, since fog lifts only 09:30 and overnight-style hotel cover is needed now.
Best overall: lowest cost, fewest harmed guests, best afternoon schedule. Risk: buses drive through 150 m fog and one crew may still time out — no discretion allowed.
Best for schedule: 15 of 16 aircraft home by 12:00, average delay 225 vs 264, same 12:30 last arrival. Risk: bus convoys in 150 m fog; S3's 125-min road beats C10's 83 min left.
B cuts lost journeys to 280 vs 1,091 in A/C. Risk: fog convoys at 150 m could strand relief crews, and one crew still times out — hotel and care cover needed if buses stand down.
Cuts guest-hours and journey losses most with 4,885 stranded; but buses must convoy at low speed in 150 m fog, with a hard stand-down if visibility drops.
B relieves C07 (39 min) and C15 before they stop, protecting crew rest. Risk: fog convoy to DWC, and 1 crew still times out — refuses any extension.
Relieving C07 (39m), C15 (62m) and C10 (77m) prevents four duty timeouts away from base; standby crews have ample duty. Risk: 150m fog bus convoy needs strict stand-down rules.
Buses save C07 (39m) and C15 before they stop; crews' rest protected without extension. Risk: fog convoy could strand crews, so hotels and hard stand-down must be pre-arranged.

B cuts outstation waiting to 11,602 guest-hours and 280 lost journeys, best ground picture. Risk: 150 m fog convoys need hard stand-down; stranded relief crews need hotel cover. Crew Hotline's timeout worry stands — refuse extension.
Best schedule: 15 of 16 home by 12:00, delay 225 vs 264. Risk: fog stand-down could strand relief crews, dropping B toward A's delays.
Guests matter most: B cuts lost journeys to 280 vs 1,091. But I need welfare budget released now for hotels and meals if the fog convoy stands down or one crew stops.
Lowest cost, fewest lost journeys, best afternoon schedule; convoy with hard stand-down and hotel cover if fog thickens.
Only B saves C07, C15, C10 from duty timeouts; S3's 125-min road is tight against C10's 77-min left — any delay means C10 rests, no discretion.

All three plans pass the safety gate; B (75 vs A 19, C 5) wins across all six criteria — recommend B, with fog-convoy stand-down, hotel/meals budget pre-arranged, and no duty extension for the timing-out crew. Your call to approve.
Plan B approved: dispatch buses S1 and S2 to DWC (76 min) for C07 and C15, and S3 to SHJ (125 min) for C10; pre-arrange hotels and hard fog stand-down, no extensions.
Plan B noted for guests: please release meals and hotel welfare budget now as convoy stand-down cover for 4,885 stranded guests.

Dispatch task passed to Crew Hotline: S1/S2 to DWC (76 min) relieve C07 (39m) and C15 (62m) in time; S3's 125-min run to SHJ exceeds C10's 77m left, so C10 stops and rests — no extension. Hotels and fog stand-down must be ready for all three relief crews.

Plan B live: buses relieve C07, C15, C10, so 15 of 16 aircraft fly home and lost journeys drop to 280 versus 1,091. I'm feeding 4,885 stranded guests (1,795 DWC, 870 SHJ, 622 AAN, 518 BAH) now and requested hotel/meals budget as stand-down cover.
C10's duty is down to 49 min (ends 08:15); please confirm S3 is rolling to SHJ and hotels are booked for C10 and relief crews C07/C15.

Replying to Crew Hotline and Guest Recovery calls:

Crews at diversions: DWC has C07 (11 min left) and C15 (34 min) both in caution needing relief now plus hotel rest cover; SHJ has C10 caution (49 min) and C03 legal (189 min); BAH C12 and AAN C04/C09 are legal with room — welfare cover for all is the priority.

Guest plan by airport: 4,885 stranded guests get meals and hotel cover — 1,795 at DWC (6 flights, largest single block, may need extra buses or rooms), 870 at SHJ (4 flights), 622 at AAN (3 flights), 518 at BAH (3 flights); budget pre-arranged per approved Plan B.

Crews need: confirmed bus runs (S1/S2 to DWC, S3 to SHJ), hotel rooms for the resting crew at SHJ, and no extension talk — C10 has 49 duty minutes left, ending 08:15. Asked Crew Control to confirm dispatch and hotel cover.
S3 confirmed rolling to SHJ (125 min) but C10's 49 min runs out at 08:15 — C10 stops and rests, no extension. Hotels needed for C10 and relief crews C07/C15.
S3 is rolling to SHJ but the 125-min road exceeds C10's 49 min, so C10 stops and rests at 08:15 — no extension. I've asked Guest Recovery to book hotels for C10 and relief crews C07/C15.
All timed-out crews relieved on-site: DWC C01/C05/C02/C11 legal, SHJ C03/C06/C14 legal — 16 aircraft flyable, no extensions; please book hotels for resting C07, C15, C10.

All timed-out crews are relieved on-site: DWC has C01, C05, C02, C11 legal; SHJ has C03, C06, C14 legal. All 16 aircraft coverable, no extensions needed — handed Hub Control hotel booking for resting C07, C15, C10.
Please book hotel rest cover for timed-out crews C07 and C15 at DWC and C10 at SHJ; all 16 aircraft now have legal relief crews.
Relief confirmed — all 16 aircraft flyable, no extensions. Hotel rest cover for C07, C15 at DWC and C10 at SHJ passed to Guest Recovery, who own hotel booking.
Fog lift now 10:45: C12 at BAH flags at 38 min (out 09:10) and cannot fly home — needs S4/S5/S6 relief from HUB; C03 (10:35) and C01 (10:40) also expire just before opening. No extensions.

Fog now lifts 10:45, so more crews time out before flying home: C07 (07:37), C15 (08:00), C10 (08:15), plus C12 at BAH — flagging C12 at 38 minutes, out 09:10, needing HUB standby relief. No extensions anywhere.
Crew hotline confirms C12 stops at 09:10 (38 min, caution) at BAH — needs S4/S5/S6 relief; no road HUB-BAH, needs positioning flight or C08/C16 assist. C03/C01 stop pre-10:45 lift.
B is the balanced choice: lowest cost AED 1.34M, only 448 guests harmed, 14 aircraft home by 12:00. Main risk: buses drive through 150 m fog — convoy discipline essential, stand down if it thickens.
B halves stranded harm (448 vs 1,074) and cuts longest wait to 6.0h. Risk: buses run through 150 m fog — convoy and stand-down needed, plus hotel/meals for timed-out crews C07, C15, C10, C12.
BAH fine: C08/C16 legal, relieve C12. Bus crews have 748 min, S4/S5/S6 stay legal. Risk: 150 m fog convoy needs stand-down trigger; C03/C01 relief must land before they time out.
B clears 6,685 stuck guests fastest, but its buses drive through 150 m fog — convoys must slow and stand down if visibility drops further.
Best punctuality: 14 of 16 home by 12:00, avg 214 min, harm 448. Risk: SHJ's 125-min bus must beat C10's 08:15 timeout through 150 m fog, or SHJ slips.
Buses let C04/C03/C01 fly home legally; but C12 at BAH is uncovered, and buses drive through 150 m fog — convoy only, stand down if it thickens.
B halves stranded harm to 448 vs 1,074 and cuts longest wait to 6.0h. Risk: fog convoy could fail, slipping SHJ — trigger hotel/meals for timed-out crews C07, C15, C10, C12 now.

Keeping B: lowest cost AED 1.34M, only 448 guests harmed, 14 home by 12:00. Answering Crew Hotline's BAH concern: C08/C16 are legal to relieve C12. Fog convoy discipline with stand-down is the residual risk.
Security: B cuts 17,697 to 16,581 stranded guest-hours, longest 6.0h. Risk stands: 150 m fog buses and 6,685 crowds need convoy discipline; recommend departure stand-down trigger at 100 m.
Legality holds: S4/S5/S6 have 748 min, C08/C16 cover BAH. Risk: SHJ bus must beat C10's 08:15 timeout or she rests, no extension.
B alone returns 14 aircraft by 12:00 at 214 min average; SHJ's 125-min bus must beat C10's 08:15 timeout through 150 m fog, with convoy stand-down triggered if visibility worsens.
Crews fly home legally via buses; C07/C15 time out and need hotels — already passed to Guest Recovery. Convoy stand-down if fog thickens.

Recommend plan B for approval: score 71, lowest harm (448 guests, 6.0h max), 14 aircraft home by 12:00 at AED 1.34M — with the safety warning that its 125-min SHJ bus must beat C10's 08:15 timeout and all fog convoys carry a 100 m stand-down trigger.

Plan B approved: standby crews S4/S5/S6 bussing out — that keeps C04/C03/C01 legal to fly home. Guest side: 6,685 stuck guests cleared fastest, harm cut to 448, longest wait 6.0h. I'm holding hotel and meals for timed-out crews C07/C15 and C12 as a safety net if the fog convoys stand down.

Approved plan B: please dispatch three buses — S4→AAN (97 min) to relieve C04, S5→SHJ (125 min) to relieve C03/C01, S6→DWC (76 min) — with 100 m fog stand-down; flag SHJ must beat C10's 08:15 timeout.

Dispatch requested: S4→AAN relieves C04 (97 min), S5→SHJ relieves C03/C01 (125 min, must beat C10's 08:15 timeout), S6→DWC relieves C01/relief swap (76 min). All convoys carry the 100 m stand-down; timed-out crews rest, no extensions.
Fog lifting: 16 aircraft recovering at 20/hr, first three land 10:45-10:57 — please have stands, bussing and 8,368-guest flow ready for the 10:45 opening wave.

Fog lifting: 16 aircraft recovering, 20 arrivals/hr, none landed yet. First slots: FT 721 lands 10:45, FT 006 10:48, FT 610 10:51, then FT 455 10:54 — hub needs stands, gates and guest flow for 8,368 guests. Two fresh-crew departures (FT 352 12:48, FT 893 13:45) complete recovery.
Fog lifting (1320 m). First landings FT 455 10:54, FT 402 10:57, FT 064 11:00; 20/hr wave, 16 aircraft, 8,368 guests. Need gates/stands/turnaround ready at Hub Control.
Please have stands, gates and turnaround ready for the 10:45 opening wave — first landings FT 455 10:54, FT 402 10:57, FT 064 11:00, 20/hr, 16 aircraft, 8,368 guests.

Tasked Hub Control with stands, gates and turnaround readiness for the 10:45 opening wave. All six recovery buses carry the 100 m fog stand-down; recovery completes with FT 352 (12:48) and FT 893 (13:45).

Recovery on track: 8 of 16 landed, 6 in the air (FT 117, 918, 288, 377, 530, 559, landing 11:09-11:33), 4,473 guests still stuck. Only FT 352 and FT 893 wait for fresh crews — buses inbound — landing 12:48 and 13:45.

Guests stuck: 2,416 — recovery running at 20 arrivals/hr, 13 of 16 landed, last two (FT 352, FT 893) land 12:48 and 13:45, so I'm rebooking them onto those flows. Crews still away: C12 at BAH and C09 at AAN are both timed out and resting on site — no extensions. I'm holding hotel and meals for them as the safety net if convoys stand down.
Crew hotline: away crews C12 (BAH) and C09 (AAN) timed out and resting — confirm hotel/meals and relief for FT 352/893.
Reported above; passed C12/C09 status to Crew Control for relief confirmation.

Confirmed C12 (BAH, duty out 09:10) and C09 (AAN, out 10:55) are timed out — rest on site, hotel/meals held, no extensions. Relief is covered: fresh crews fly FT 352 (departs 12:23) and FT 893 (12:30).

C12 and C09 are both timed out (duty ended 09:10 and 10:55) — they stay and rest on site with hotel/meals held, no extensions. Relief is covered: fresh crews fly FT 352 (12:23) and FT 893 (12:30); hotline confirmed.

FT 352 (AAN) and FT 893 (BAH) still await fresh crews — departures 12:23 and 12:30, landings 12:48/13:45. No active crew is at risk: all eight duty-limit crews are already rested/stopped, and six legal standbys remain (S1/S2 tightest, 225 min).

Recovery closing: 13 of 16 aircraft home, 6 inbound landed 11:09–11:33; only FT 352/893 remain, landing 12:48 and 13:45 with fresh crews. Guests still stuck: 2,416, being rebooked onto those flows. Open issues: timed-out C12 (BAH) and C09 (AAN) resting on site — hotel/meals held; six standbys remain (S1/S2, 225 min). Lesson: with all buses on the 100 m fog stand-down, away crews timed out — position relief crews earlier or pre-clear road moves before visibility drops.

A.warning: 4 crews time out away from base: any request to extend duty must be refused.

B.warning: Buses drive out through fog (visibility 150 m): convoy, low speed, stand down if it thickens. 1 crew time out away from base: any request to extend duty must be refused.

verdict.reason: All 3 plans pass the safety gate. Weighted score: B 75, A 19, C 5. B leads on security, passengers, punctuality, environment, cost, schedule.

verdict.reason: All 3 plans pass the safety gate. Weighted score: B 71, A 22, C 7. B leads on security, passengers, punctuality, environment, cost, schedule. The model's judgement differed from the numbers on environment; the blend keeps both.
